page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-240GB-1xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor and the x86_64 architecture. It features 12 shared vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 240.0 GB of system memory. The primary hardware accelerator is a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU equipped with 80 GB of VRAM. This server does not include local storage, meaning external storage solutions must be attached.

Benchmark results indicate strong capabilities in specific single-threaded and multi-threaded operations. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 35.51 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scored in the top tier at 15.51 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 182.09 GB/sec. For AI workloads, the NVIDIA H100 GPU delivered top-tier LLM inference performance on a small 135M model, processing prompts at 10515.12 tokens/sec and generating text at 547.27 tokens/sec. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks, such as stress-ng and PassMark, generally fall within the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density by pairing a premium enterprise GPU with a massive 240.0 GB memory footprint, which translates to 20.0 GB of RAM per core. However, a notable tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce performance variability under sustained multi-tenant CPU loads. Additionally, the lack of local storage requires users to budget for and configure network-attached storage.

This configuration is highly suited for deep learning, artificial intelligence model inference, and data science tasks that leverage GPU acceleration and require a large memory capacity. It is also appropriate for memory-intensive data processing, scientific simulations, and parallel decompression tasks, while being less optimal for workloads requiring dedicated, non-shared CPU cores or high-speed local NVMe storage.
